determinism.method: The scorer's verdict is a pure function of the served bytes plus the ported predicate, and the port is sha256-pinned to the primary (CategoryViewTree.tsx:135-139) so a drifted primary makes the tool REFUSE rather than score against a stale copy. The renders were repeated: global and inflection were each rendered more than once in this session, and the earlier pair was re-run from the COMMITTED state against a freshly restarted server.
determinism.observed: STABLE on the subject. Repeated renders reproduced identical values, colours, ordering and layout. A sha256 of the PNG pairs DIFFERS and is recorded here as a REJECTED ORACLE, not a failure: the captures are full-page and the analytics panel above the subject carries its own dynamic content, so a whole-page byte hash answers 'are these bytes identical', not 'does this component draw the same thing'. Reporting that DIFFERS as a determinism failure would have been a wrong-instrument verdict on a correct render.
